 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Portland Trail Blazers have quickly emerged as one of the NBA's more impressive teams to begin the 2026-27 season. At 3-1, Portland has already shown that its offseason additions have made a significant difference, but Saturday's road matchup against the Utah Jazz presents a new challenge. With Ja Morant sidelined for at least several weeks, the Blazers will get their first extended look at how this roster operates without one of its most important playmakers.
 How to Watch
 Date: Saturday, October 31
 Time (PT): 12:00 PM
 TV: Rip City Television Network or BlazerVision
 Location: Delta Center | Salt Lake City, UT
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Game Outlook
 Portland's early success has been built around something that wasn't always present last season: balance.
 A year ago, Deni Avdija was frequently asked to carry a significant portion of the offensive workload. He emerged as one of the league's more intriguing young players, but there were nights when the Trail Blazers simply didn't have enough complementary scoring and playmaking around him.
 That hasn't been the case to begin this season.
 The additions of Ja Morant and Damian Lillard have given Portland more offensive options, while Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson provide additional backcourt depth. Instead of relying on one player to create everything, the Blazers have been able to attack opponents in several different ways.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement That depth will now be tested.
 Morant suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain in Thursday's loss to the Memphis Grizzlies and is expected to miss at least four weeks. It's an unfortunate development for a team that had been building momentum, especially with Shaedon Sharpe already sidelined following offseason knee surgery.
 Still, Portland has the personnel to remain competitive without Morant. Lillard has looked excellent in his return to the court, and his ability to score and facilitate will become even more important over the coming weeks. Holiday brings veteran stability, while Henderson has an opportunity to earn a larger role.
 Avdija should also benefit from the team's improved supporting cast, even with Morant unavailable. The offense may look different without Morant's ability to attack the paint and draw defensive attention, but Portland has enough capable players to continue generating quality looks.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Saturday's opponent is dealing with even more significant injury concerns. Utah is just 1-4 and has lost three consecutive games, with Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkic both sidelined. That leaves the Jazz particularly vulnerable in the frontcourt, where Donovan Clingan could have an opportunity to make a significant impact.
 The Blazers are favored by multiple possessions, and that line feels appropriate given how the two teams have performed thus far. Portland has the better record, more proven depth and a roster that has already demonstrated its ability to win games in different ways.
 The bigger question isn't necessarily whether Portland has enough talent to beat Utah. It's whether the Blazers can maintain their offensive rhythm without Morant and continue building on what has been an encouraging start to the season.
 Betting Odds
 Spread: Trail Blazers -6.5 (-106)
 Moneyline: Trail Blazers -235
 Over/Under: 231.5 (-110)
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Following this contest, the Trail Blazers will continue their road trip against the Denver Nuggets on Monday, November 2, in another early test against Western Conference competition.
